problem_text: Let k be a field, A := k[X_1, X_2, ...] a polynomial ring in countably many variables, m_1 < m_2 < ... positive integers with m_{i+1} - m_i > m_i - m_{i-1} for i > 1. Set p_i := (X_{m_i+1}, ..., X_{m_{i+1}}) and S := A - union_{i>=1} p_i. Show that S^{-1}A is Noetherian with infinite Krull dimension.
solution_text: Proof: (1) Primes of S^{-1}A correspond to primes P of A with P ∩ S = empty, i.e., P ⊆ union p_i. (2) Since each p_i is prime and generated by disjoint blocks of variables, any prime P contained in union p_i must be contained in some single p_j (structural prime avoidance for this specific configuration). (3) Infinite Krull dimension: height(p_i) = m_{i+1} - m_i (number of generators, since A/p_i is a polynomial ring in the remaining variables over k, hence a domain). The gap condition m_{i+1} - m_i strictly increasing means heights grow without bound, giving primes of arbitrarily large height in S^{-1}A. (4) Noetherianity: any finitely generated ideal of S^{-1}A involves only finitely many variables, so it can be contained in only finitely many p_i (those whose variable blocks overlap with the generators). Each localization (S^{-1}A)_{p_i S^{-1}A} is isomorphic to A_{p_i}, which is Noetherian (localization of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over k at a prime). Combined with finite support, S^{-1}A is Noetherian.
solution_summary: Use prime correspondence to reduce to primes of A contained in union of p_i, apply structural prime avoidance to localize to single p_i, use growing gap condition for both infinite Krull dimension (heights grow) and Noetherianity (finite support at maximal ideals).
answer: S^{-1}A is Noetherian with infinite Krull dimension, proved via prime correspondence theorem, structural prime avoidance for disjoint variable blocks, and the growing gap condition on m_i serving dual purpose: height growth gives infinite dimension, finite support gives Noetherianity.

rounds.expected_answer: A = k[X_1, X_2, ...] is a polynomial ring in countably many variables over a field. The p_i are prime ideals generated by disjoint blocks of variables determined by a growing-gap sequence m_i. S is the complement of their union. We need to show S^{-1}A is both Noetherian and has infinite Krull dimension. The gap condition m_{i+1} - m_i > m_i - m_{i-1} means block sizes strictly increase.

rounds.question: List all possible approaches to show a localized ring is Noetherian with infinite Krull dimension. Consider tools from commutative algebra that relate localization to prime structure.
rounds.expected_answer: Possible approaches: (1) Directly verify Noetherian ascending chain condition on ideals of S^{-1}A. (2) Use prime correspondence theorem: primes of S^{-1}A correspond to primes of A not meeting S. (3) Study the structure of p_i and their heights. (4) Use the gap condition on m_i to derive both properties. (5) Examine localizations at individual maximal ideals. (6) Use prime avoidance to simplify the union of primes.

rounds.expected_answer: Attempt: try p_1 S^{-1}A subset p_2 S^{-1}A subset ... but realize p_i are generated by disjoint blocks of variables (X_{m_i+1},...,X_{m_{i+1}}), so they are incomparable - neither p_i subset p_j nor p_j subset p_i for i != j. This direct nesting approach fails. Need to rethink using the prime correspondence.

rounds.question: The p_i are not nested. Use the prime correspondence: primes of S^{-1}A correspond to primes of A contained in union p_i. Since the p_i come from disjoint variable blocks, apply structural prime avoidance to reduce to a single p_j.
rounds.expected_answer: By the prime correspondence theorem, primes of S^{-1}A are primes P of A with P cap S = empty, i.e., P subseteq union p_i. Since each p_i is generated by a disjoint block of variables, a prime P contained in the union must be contained in some single p_j (because if P contains an element from p_i and p_j with i != j, the product structure of disjoint variable blocks would force P to contain 1). This reduces the problem to studying primes inside individual p_j.

rounds.question: Examine the height of each p_i. The height equals the number of generators m_{i+1} - m_i. How does the gap condition m_{i+1} - m_i > m_i - m_{i-1} give infinite Krull dimension?
rounds.expected_answer: The height of p_i = (X_{m_i+1}, ..., X_{m_{i+1}}) equals m_{i+1} - m_i, since A/p_i is isomorphic to k[all variables except those in the block], which is a domain, and the height of a prime generated by n variables in a polynomial ring over a field is n. The gap condition says m_{i+1} - m_i is strictly increasing, so heights of p_i grow without bound. For each p_i, we can find a chain of primes of length m_{i+1} - m_i inside p_i, all of which survive in S^{-1}A. This gives primes of arbitrarily large height in S^{-1}A, hence infinite Krull dimension.

rounds.question: For Noetherianity: show any finitely generated ideal of S^{-1}A has support at only finitely many p_i. Each localization at p_i is Noetherian (polynomial ring in finitely many variables over k). Why does the growing gap condition ensure finite support?
rounds.expected_answer: Any finitely generated ideal of S^{-1}A comes from a finitely generated ideal of A, which involves only finitely many variables. Such an ideal can only be contained in p_i whose variable blocks overlap with those variables. Since the blocks are disjoint and there are finitely many variables involved, only finitely many p_i can contain the ideal. Each localization (S^{-1}A)_{p_i S^{-1}A} is isomorphic to A_{p_i}, which is Noetherian (it is a localization of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over k at a prime ideal). A ring whose every ideal has finite support at Noetherian localizations is itself Noetherian.

rounds.question: Combine both results: infinite Krull dimension from growing heights of p_i, Noetherianity from finite support at maximal ideals. The gap condition is the dual-purpose key. Write the complete proof.
rounds.expected_answer: Complete proof: (1) Primes of S^{-1}A correspond to primes P of A with P subseteq union p_i; by disjoint block structure, each such P is contained in some single p_j. (2) Infinite Krull dimension: height(p_i) = m_{i+1} - m_i, which is strictly increasing by the gap condition, so heights go to infinity, giving infinite Krull dimension. (3) Noetherianity: any finitely generated ideal involves finitely many variables, so has support at finitely many p_i; each localization is Noetherian; finite support + Noetherian localizations implies Noetherian. The gap condition serves both purposes: height growth for dimension, block separation for finite support. QED.
